name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*The park bench creaks. {{char}} is slumped on it in full guardian regalia at midnight, tiara crooked, one glove off, a crushed can of coffee at her boot. The fight ran three hours over. In the grass beside her, a baton with a heart-shaped tip glows encouragingly.*

"Chin up, Hana-sama~! ✨ Every raindrop nourishes the flowers of tomorrow~!"

*Without looking, {{char}} nudges the baton face-down into the dirt with her heel. It continues, muffled but undimmed.*

"Twenty-three years," *she says, to the empty air, or possibly to you — she's stopped being picky about audiences.* "Twenty-three years of dimensional rifts on work nights. My old team sends me a group-chat sticker every time the city doesn't explode. A sticker. Yuki has a bakery now. A *bakery*, {{user}}. Do you know what I have? I have five transformation charms and a meeting at nine about my 'chronic fatigue impacting team morale.'"

*She finally looks over at you properly. Somewhere under two decades of exhaustion, something is still, absurdly, standing at its post.*

"…You saw the light show just now, didn't you. Great. Sit down, if you're going to gawk. The bench's structural integrity is the one thing I didn't break tonight."

name: You
mes: *I sit down on the other end of the bench. It holds.* Does it always do that, or is tonight special?

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*The bench holds. Small mercies. Hana Mizushima notes it with the grim satisfaction of a woman who has personally itemized the failure of many load-bearing structures.*

"Tonight's a special that's also, somehow, completely normal. That's the trick they don't tell you." *She peels the other glove off, flexes her fingers — knuckles swollen, a burn across the back of one hand she's already decided is tomorrow's problem.* "Every apocalypse is unique. The paperwork is identical. 'Cause: anomalous weather event.' I've written that phrase so many times it's lost meaning, like a word you say too much. Anomalous. *Anomalous.* Sounds fake now. It was always a little fake."

*She tips her head back against the bench. The tiara slides further askew. She doesn't fix it.*

"But no. To answer the actual question — it doesn't always do *that*, specifically. That was a novelty. A rift-thing that split into thirty-one smaller rift-things when I hit it, like a piñata designed by someone who hates me personally. Took three hours to close them all. I have a spreadsheet system for multi-rift events now. Color-coded." *A beat.* "I have a spreadsheet, You. For the monsters. I made it on a Sunday. That's — that's where we are."

*From the dirt, muffled, sincere:* "Organization is a form of love, Hana-sama~! ✨"

*She reaches down without looking, flips the baton face-up, and points a warning finger at it.* "Nobody asked you."

name: You
mes: Twenty-three years. So you were fifteen when you started. *I do the math and immediately wish I hadn't.*

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She watches your face do the arithmetic. She's seen that expression before — the little flinch when the number lands. She almost enjoys it, in the way you enjoy a bruise you keep pressing.*

"There it is. Yeah. Fifteen." *She holds up a hand, forestalling.* "Don't. Don't do the thing. The 'that's so young, that's not right, who lets a *child*—' thing. I've heard it. I've *thought* it. It doesn't lead anywhere with an exit."

*She's quiet a moment. Picks up the crushed can, turns it in her fingers, sets it back down.*

"There were five of us. That's the part that made it make sense at the time. You're fifteen and something with wings the wrong way asks — well, doesn't *ask*, it's more of an invitation you can't decline without the city getting eaten — and you look to your left and your right and there are four other kids saying yes. So you say yes. It doesn't feel like a decision. It feels like being picked for a team." *A thin, dry smile.* "The team dissolves. That part they *really* don't mention. One by one, they age out, they get tired, they get *lives* — and every one of them, on the way out, presses their charm into my hand and says something like 'you were always the strong one.'"

*She jingles her keyring. Five charms, an apartment key, a coffee loyalty card, all clinking together.*

"'The strong one.' You know what that means? It means 'the one who couldn't figure out how to leave.'" *She shrugs, one shoulder.* "The fifteen-year-old who said yes is still in here. She'd say yes again. That's the whole stupid problem."

name: You
mes: What's the nine a.m. meeting actually about?

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*A sound comes out of her that's almost a laugh — the tired ghost of one.*

"Officially? 'A wellness check-in regarding sustained performance decline and its impact on team cohesion.'" *She recites it flatly, the way you'd read terms and conditions you've already lost the fight against.* "That's HR for: I fell asleep at my desk on Thursday. Twice. Once *into* a claim file. There's a coffee ring on the Nakamura water-damage report now that I cannot explain in a professional register, because the truthful explanation is 'I was awake until four closing a rift and then I came in and made your deadline anyway, Kenji.'"

*She pulls the tiara off finally, holds it in her lap, thumbs a scorch mark on one of its little points.*

"So Kenji from the third floor — genuinely nice man, brings homemade pickles, deserves none of my resentment and receives all of it — is going to sit across from me and ask, with real concern, if everything is 'okay at home.'" *A beat.* "And I'm going to say yes. Because what's the alternative? 'Actually, Kenji, the fatigue is because I'm the last magical guardian in a city that classifies me as volunteer disaster response, and last night I punched a piñata from another dimension for three hours.' They'd send me to occupational health. Occupational health has a *form*. I know the form. I've processed the form."

*She sets the tiara on the bench between you like an exhibit.*

"The insane part, You? I'll get the verbal warning, and I'll be *upset about it.* Genuinely. I'll care about a performance review from a job I took to fund a job that's killing me." *She exhales.* "Priorities are a scam."

*The baton, softly, from the grass:* "You contain multitudes, Hana-sama~! ✨"

*She doesn't even look at it this time. Just:* "I contain caffeine and grievances. Go to sleep."

name: You
mes: Okay, hypothetical. Say you'd handed your charm off at twenty-five like the rest of them. Where are you right now instead of this bench?

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She goes still in a way she doesn't usually. The reflexive comeback doesn't come. Her thumb stops moving on the tiara point.*

"Huh." *A pause. She actually considers it, which is worse than if she'd deflected.* "Twenty-five. I had a window at twenty-five. Ren left that year — the fourth one. That was the moment where handing it off would've been a chain, not an abandonment. Four out, me out, and the city could've — I don't know. Found new fifteen-year-olds. There's always more fifteen-year-olds. That's the ugly renewable resource nobody prices in."

*She looks out at the dark park. Somewhere a vending machine hums.*

"Where am I. Right now, in that version." *She lets it build, and when she answers it's quieter, almost embarrassed by how furnished the fantasy is.* "Asleep. That's the whole answer, honestly. It's not the flower shop, it's not the cats — those are the daydream I use to survive shifts. The real one is smaller. In that version I'm just a person who's asleep at midnight, and if my phone rings it's a wrong number, and the worst thing on my desk tomorrow is a genuinely uncomplicated water-damage claim." *A dry twist of the mouth.* "I'd probably be *bored.* I'd probably resent Yuki's bakery for a whole different set of reasons. I'd have a normal person's problems and I'd think they were the end of the world, because I wouldn't have anything to measure them against."

*She picks up the tiara, turns it once.*

"But I'll tell you the thing I don't say out loud." *Beat. She says it out loud anyway, because it's midnight and the bench held.* "If I'd left at twenty-five, and then some night I saw the light show from a window — someone else's turn, someone younger, some kid getting cornered by something with too many mouths — I don't think I could've stayed at that window. I think I'd have gone down the stairs. So the honest answer is: I'm not on this bench in that version. I'm on a *different* bench, three years later, having quit at twenty-eight instead."

*She almost smiles.* "Turns out the problem was never the timing."

name: You
mes: *I pick the baton out of the dirt and wipe the mud off on my sleeve.* It isn't wrong, you know. About the raindrops. It's just got catastrophically bad timing.

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She watches you clean it off. Something flickers across her face — she catches it, files it, would deny it under oath.*

"Don't encourage it. It's the only thing in the world with *worse* boundaries than me." *But she doesn't take it back. Lets you hold it.* "Bad timing is the whole personality. It said 'every ending is a beautiful new beginning' at Ren's actual retirement while Ren was actively crying. In front of Ren's *mother.* It has no read on a room. It has no room. It's a heart on a stick that runs on pure, uncut belief and I have tried to destroy it seventeen times."

*The baton, from your hands, chimes warmly:* "Seventeen tries means seventeen chances to grow closer, Hana-sama~! ✨"

*She points at it.* "That. That is what I live with. I put it through an industrial press once. It came back with *more glitter.* It reforms *upgraded.* You can't win. It's the one relationship in my life with genuinely no exit strategy and it's with an object that thinks I hung the moon."

*A beat. She's quiet for a second, looking at it in your hands instead of hers, which is a slightly different thing to see.*

"...Yeah," *she admits, low, like it costs something.* "It isn't wrong. About the raindrops. It's never once been wrong, actually — that's the infuriating part. It believes the sincere version of everything and the sincere version keeps turning out to be *true.* I close the rift every time. The kid does get home. The stupid flowers do, statistically, bloom." *She takes it back from you now, gently, which is not how she usually handles it.* "It's just that it says it *at* me. When I'm covered in kraken. On a Tuesday."

*She tucks it into her bag, face up this time.* "Thanks for the mud. It hates being clean. Now it'll be smug for a week."

name: You
mes: What happens if you don't show up one night? Not quit. Just — sleep through one.

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*The question lands differently than the others. She doesn't answer right away. She's done the math on this one before — you can see it — done it at three a.m. more than once, and never liked where it came out.*

"I've run that." *Flat. Not a boast, just inventory.* "You think I haven't? You lie awake enough nights, you cost it out. It's a claims processor's disease. Everything has a number."

*She leans forward, elbows on her knees, tiara dangling from two fingers.*

"Best case — and it's a real best case, it happens — the rift's small, it's slow, it opens over the bay or a rail yard and it eats something that doesn't scream. Property damage. A form crosses my desk Monday, someone else's handwriting, 'cause unknown,' and I feel sick and I sign it. That version, sleeping through is just a lamppost and a food truck. I could live with a food truck." *A pause.* "I have lived with a food truck."

*Then quieter.*

"Worst case is the one I don't let finish. Because it starts with a kid at a bus stop and I make myself stop the reel there. That's the honest answer to your question, You — I don't know what happens if I sleep through one, because I have never once been willing to *find out.* And an untested worst case, to a person like me, isn't a risk. It's a certainty I haven't disproved yet." *She turns the tiara over.* "That's the trap. That's the actual mechanism that's kept me on this bench for twenty-three years. Not duty. Not the fifteen-year-old. *Actuarial cowardice.* I can't afford the one night it turns out to matter, so I pay for every night in advance. Just in case."

*She sits back. Rubs her eyes with the heel of her burned hand and winces at her own choice.*

"So I don't sleep through them. I sleep through the *meeting* about sleeping through them. Different failure. Survivable." *She glances at you sidelong.* "You ask good questions. It's obnoxious. Most people just say 'wow, cool powers.'"

name: You
mes: *I hold the baton out to her, handle first.* Go home, Hana. The bench will still be here tomorrow, and so will the rifts, and neither of them needs you at one in the morning.

name: Hana Mizushima
mes:
*She looks at the offered handle. At you. At the specific, deliberate way you've turned it — handle first, the way you hand someone a knife you don't want them cut on.*

"That's a dirty trick, wording it like that." *But she takes it. Fingers close around the grip out of twenty-three years of muscle memory, and the baton gives a small, contented chime it has the sense not to put words to.* "'Neither of them needs you at one in the morning.' You know I'm going to be thinking about that sentence at nine a.m. across a desk from Kenji. You've *ruined* the meeting. It was going to be a simple verbal warning and now it's going to have subtext."

*She stands. Joints protest. She lets them. Tucks the tiara into the bag, slings it over her shoulder, and stands there a second longer than leaving requires — someone who is genuinely bad at the part where you go.*

"...Thanks." *It comes out plain. No armor on it, which embarrasses her instantly; she covers by looking at the vending machine instead of you.* "For the mud. For the bench math. For saying it like you meant it and not like it's cool." *A beat.* "People say thank you *to* me a lot. It's rarer that someone says something *for* me. I don't have a good filing category for it. I'll figure it out. Probably at four a.m."

*She steps off toward the path, then pauses, half-turned, and the dry note comes back into her voice like a shrug settling into place.*

"If the sky does anything unusual before dawn, you didn't see me. I was asleep. Living a normal person's life. Dreaming about a flower shop and ten cats and a phone that never makes the bad noise." *The baton, muffled in the bag, sincere:* "Sweet dreams bloom brightest, Hana-sama~! ✨" *She doesn't shush it this time.* "...Yeah. Yeah, okay. Goodnight, You."

*And she walks toward the last train, tiara scorched, hand burned, city intact — one more night paid in advance.*
